steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Place the blueberries in the pastry shell and set aside.
Combine 1 cup sugar, 1/3 cup flour, and salt. Add eggs and sour cream, stirring until blended. Pour the sour cream custard over the blueberries.

In another bowl, combine 1/2 cup sugar and 1/2 cup flour. Cut in the butter with pastry blender until the mixture resembles coarse meal. Sprinkle the topping over the sour cream mixture and berries in the pie shell.
Bake in the preheated oven for 50 to 55 minutes, or until lightly browned. Cool on wire rack.

raw_recipe.headline: Creamy Blueberry Pie
raw_recipe.description: A sweet, custardy sour cream mixture is spooned over fresh blueberries, topped with a sweet buttery crumble, and baked. If desired, garnish with mint sprigs and additional blueberries.
raw_recipe.name: Creamy Blueberry Pie

review.reviewBody: Lets say you're escaping from LV 426 but right before you do, a warrior steals this Creamy Blueberry Pie. He takes it down to sub level 2 in the atmospheric processor and places it in a cocoon. A nuclear explosion is about to go off and you only have 14 minutes to reach minimum safe distance all while the Queen is right behind you. DO YOU GO AFTER YOUR STOLEN PIE? Yes. You should also go after it even if the blueberries have been substituted for a mixed berries. Because that's delicious too. After you eat, you might be wondering if you can dream. My answer would be: I-Firmative.

This is my go to pie. It’s really really really yummy. I make it with fresh blueberries or fresh pitted whole cherries or peaches or raspberries or a mix of berries of even frozen berries. Make two when you make it because you will want one pie all to yourself. I follow the recipe as is using a scant amount less sugar. I also find that I need to cover the edges of the crust the last 20 minutes of cooking. This pie will make you famous!

I made a bunch of changes, but started with this recipe that is a game changer. Probably I’ll add the new concoction as a separate recipe, eventually.

First made a blueberry pie filling, simmered 1-1/2 containers of blueberries with 1/4c water, 1/4c cherry juice, 1/2t vanilla, 1/3c white sugar, 1T cornstarch.

Didn’t have enough blueberries, so greased a 5x8 pan.
Didn’t have a pie crust so made double the crumble (half white sugar, half brown sugar, lots of butter) and used half as the bottom crust. Baked the bottom crust for 10 minutes at 400. 
Added 1t cinnamon to the custard and cut the sugar in half.
Layered the crumble over the custard over the blueberry filling and baked for 25 minutes.
So. Amazingly. Wonderful. (with vanilla ice cream)

I have made this particular recipe on numerous occasions. it usually turns out very well, and there are usually no leftovers. I use half the amount of sugar in the custard base, and I use three quarters of the sugar in the buttery crust. Do not use fully frozen blueberries or use too much sour cream in the custard sauce. This will cause your pie to have a soupy texture. I use two and two thirds cups of blueberries per pie. I have found that using three in the pre-made pie shells that I use tends to overfill them. This last time placed crushed walnuts on top of the pie after I had sprinkled the buttery topping. it turned out phenomenally well. perhaps some of these suggestions May help you but I definitely would recommend cutting back on the sugar as it does not usually dissolve properly in the mix

Absolutely delicious!!! Use a Pillsbury frozen pie shell. Added 1 teaspoon of vanilla to custard portion and a dash of salt to the crumb topping, otherwise followed recipe. Everybody at the dinner party I brought it to said it was so good. Cooked mine 1 hr 15 minutes until it really looked like it was browning on top and on the sides of the crust. It puffed a bit in the center. I was worried it wasn't fully done because it was a bit jiggly in the center, but it firmed up as it cooled (it fell a little in the center) but was fully cooked.

This is a great recipe! I have used the recipe several times for blueberry pie and have replaced the blueberries with chopped rhubarb, red raspberries, diced nectarines and chopped chopped apples. With the apples I added cinnamon in the filling and topping, in the nectarine pie I added almond extract in the filling and sliced almonds in the topping and lately because there are only two of us I’ve cut the recipe in half to make a six inch pie,it works perfectly. I also add lemon zest to my blueberry pies now it makes the blueberry flavor stand out more.

I made the pie exactly as recipe directs except for blind baking the crust 8 minutes and cooling before adding berries and custard plus crumb topping. 
 Defititely easy to prepare,and the berries don't get crushed. The resulting pie is lovely, but so sweet I had a hard time swallowing even with unsweetened coffee. The topping actually crunched with sugar. That might be caused by the organic sugar I used, as I have noticed the crystal structure takes longer to disolve than the popular store brand. I found I had more crumble than needed but put it all on the pie anyway. Next time I will reduce the sugar in topping from 1/2 cup to 1/4 cup, and from 1 cup to 2/3 cup for the sugar in custard mixture. Meanwhile, I include a dollop of sour cream on the plate so I can add some to each bite to temper the sweetness. It's actually quite good that way! Overall a great recipe and I will definitely be making it again!

This was a really good recipe! Friends of mine asked for more. Being unfamiliar with pie creations, I just picked this one off of previous reviews. I used exactly what the recipe called for, no substitutions other than the fact I used fresh picked blackberries instead of blueberries. When I made it the second time, I added cinnamon just because and brown sugar to the crumble. I don't own a pastry blender so I melted the butter into the flour and sugar for the crumbled topping. Great recipe!

I agree with JasonERF, if you get to a boss battle and the boss STEALS YOUR PIE/CAKE go after it. Fight long and hard, and vanquish your foe to win back your pie/cake. I made two of these July 4 alone, and all had rave reviews, using the 2/3 cup sour cream and 1/2 cup sugar ratio. You don't need the sugar, you really don't. But I did use full sour cream, not the light, and added the zest of half a lemon, as well as lemon extract because I can't afford vanilla these days. I also switched some other things up a little because I can't help myself, this evening I'm not using a pie crust at all but trying it as a sort of cobbler, with just the berries I picked with my 2 sons today and the afore mentioned lemon zest, juice and extract. It's phenomenal.

Per other cooks' recommendations I increased sour cream by a quarter cup and decrease sugar by quarter cup. I put in half brown sugar in batter and topping and added a teaspoon of cinnamon to both the batter and to the topping. Also, I parbaked the piecrust and it came out perfect!

VERY GOOD PIE!!!! Delicious warm with ice cream, or cold. 
Note to self: 5lb box of fresh blueberries makes 4 pies. Triple the custard filling; double the strusel topping (perfect amounts). Bake convection 325 for 1-hour and 10-minutes (or longer as needed till not jiggly in the middle).
ADJUSTMENTS: Custard Filling: reduce sugar to 3/4-cup, increase sour cream to 2/3-cup, add 1/4-tsp cinnamon and 1-tsp vanilla. Topping: use brown sugar instead of white, add 1-tsp cinnamon.

I followed directions to a T first time making a different type of blueberry pie ! It came out awesome and I cooked it in a cast iron skillet on a pellet grill while grilling ribs just beyond good had a little smoky flavor which highlighted the flavor
My stepdaughter made this on our family vacation and it was amazing. We ate it fresh from the oven warm and the next day cold. It is a keeper for sure! Easy to make!
Easy PEASY!! Very tasty, very simple. My only adjustment would be to reduce the amount of sugar since the amount used made it extremely sweet. Will make it again.

I have made this countless times it is very tasty! I use a graham cracker crust and cut the sugar in the custard to 3/4 cup, reading others reviews I add a tablespoon of vanilla but this last time I used lemon juice instead and we liked that too! I make it with 1/2 the crumble or no crumble at all (if I'm trying to cut calories) it's very versatile and all versions are always a hit with my family. This is the one my husband asks for when our blueberries come in and he wants me to make "something blueberry".
My husband's favorite pie!
This was very good. I really have no complaints except I found another recipe that’s not as sweet and has more flavour.

This pie was so easy to make and came out perfectly after following the recipe and directions exactly. The full flavor of the blueberries (ours were fresh picked) came through, and the texture was firm enough that the filling did not fall out when removing individual slices. The streusel topping was a perfect fit for this pie. A winner all the way around.

Excellent and easy! Reduced to 2/3 the recipe for a traditional pie crust. Added a little lemon juice to the custard. Swapped out the white sugar for brown in the streusel. Would consider reducing the sugar in the custard for next time, but was excellent as written.
Added lemon juice and cinnamon
